ENVOY: an embedding-based selection of authentic HIV-1 Env representatives for cross-clade immunogen panels

Aryan Patel · BCGE Lab · Center for Vaccine and Virology Research, HMS/BIDMC

ENVOY is a reproducible computational pipeline for selecting real, high-fitness HIV-1 Env sequences as immunogen candidates from the circulating viral population. Past HIV-1 vaccine designs built from synthetic sequences — arithmetic consensus and combinatorial mosaics — reached clinical trials (HVTN 705 Imbokodo, HVTN 706 Mosaico) and returned near-zero efficacy. The structural reason is simple: averaging a column of amino acids breaks co-evolving pairs, and splicing linear T-cell epitope fragments disrupts the quaternary packing of the native Env trimer.

ENVOY takes the opposite approach. We cluster real circulating sequences in protein language model space (ESM-2 650M mean-pool) and return the authentic medoid of each cluster — a real, high-fitness viral tip that retains native epistasis, native glycan shield, and quaternary conformation. Each medoid ships with two backup candidates in case the primary fails to express.

Pipeline

The pipeline comprises six stages, each a reproducible unit with its own output directory. Configuration is logged per stage; random seeds are deterministic.

  1. envoy qc — six gates plus the Rose & Korber Hypermut filter on raw Env FASTAs.
  2. envoy dedup — CD-HIT 98% deduplication with smart-pick representative selection.
  3. envoy embed — ESM-2 650M mean-pool embedding, GPU auto-detect (CUDA → Apple MPS → CPU).
  4. envoy cluster — PAM k-medoids at k = 20 with N+2 backup panel per medoid.
  5. envoy figures — per-clade and cross-clade publication figures.
  6. envoy divergence — identity-vs-embedding divergence analysis.

Cross-clade panel gallery

ENVOY is being deployed across 11 HIV-1 subtypes and circulating recombinant forms (A1, A6, B, C, D, G, F1, CRF01_AE, CRF02_AG, CRF07_BC, CRF08_BC). Per-clade figures are added here as each panel completes. Follow the cross-clade work in the repository.

Validation — AMP matched set

On the AMP matched set — 32 pure-Clade-B viruses from HVTN 704 for which full gp160 sequence and sensitivity data against 14 broadly neutralizing antibodies are jointly available — mean-pool ESM-2 (650M) cosine distance plus PAM k-medoids at k = 20 beats 83.4% of 10,000 random baselines on the primary antigenic treatment and 90.1% on the sensitivity treatment. Six embedding representations and two selection methods were tested; this configuration was pre-registered before any correlation was computed.

Methodological writeup

A full methods writeup covering the matched-set definition, the antigenic treatments (rank-per-bnAb primary, log10-cap-at-25 sensitivity), the Phase B representation comparison, and the k-sweep selection landscape is being prepared alongside the manuscript. Decisions and summary numbers are available in the repository notes.

Install

The pip-installable envoy-hiv package is being prepared for a 0.1.0 pre-release. Until then, ENVOY runs from a clone of the GitHub repository: 
git clone https://github.com/aryanp2107/envoy
cd envoy
# installation instructions will appear here when the package lands

Documentation

Full user guide, CLI reference, and FAQ are being written in parallel with the 0.1.0 pre-release. They will appear here as each section is ready. For now, the repository README is the current source of truth.
